packageRules.description: mise-managed toolchain tools, minor/patch/digest only — majors (e.g. node 24) need human review and must not join this group. Excludes go: also gomod-relevant, must stay standalone.

Go module minor bumps not already claimed by a package-name group below. Split from patch/digest (see go-patch below) because Renovate ANDs automerge across every member of one grouped branch — a single minor bump riding along with patch/digest deps on one branch was blocking that branch's automerge entirely. MUST stay before the package-name rules: Renovate applies packageRules in order and a later match overwrites an earlier scalar groupName, so this generic rule would silently absorb kubernetes/sigs.k8s.io/fluxcd/cloudnative-pg/internal updates if it came after them. Excludes go: keep standalone so a Go bump can't red the whole group.

Go module patch/digest bumps not already claimed by a package-name group below. Split from minor (see go-minor above) so this group never carries a minor member and stays automerge-eligible on its own via the automerge rule near the end of this array. MUST stay before the package-name rules, same reason as go-minor. Excludes go: keep standalone.
Kubernetes core. Grouping follows upstream release cadence.
sigs.k8s.io. Grouping follows upstream release cadence.
Flux controller APIs are released together and imported as one surface — never bump piecemeal.
CloudNativePG — the operator, machinery, barman-cloud and the plugin move together upstream.

First-party libraries. Never automerged: a go-kure/kure bump in a consumer repo carries release-ordering constraints (see the consumer's own guards). Downstream consumers add their own matchers for their own modules in their own config; this preset is public and stays upstream-only.
GitHub Actions bumps land as chore(ci), matching the commit convention the previous Dependabot config used.

Go itself is excluded from the groups above but must not land unreviewed — a bare Go bump fails each repo's version-consistency checks unless the repo's own sync tooling (scripts/sync-versions.sh) runs alongside it. Dashboard-gate rather than disable, so a security-relevant Go patch stays visible; ticking it still requires the manual sync. allowedVersions keeps the whole 1.27 line unproposed while 1.26 still receives security backports — lift when Go 1.28 ships.

The golang base image is the same Go toolchain as the rule above wearing its dockerfile hat — a 1.26→1.27 tag bump is classified minor, so the all-managers major gate below never catches it. Same gate, same pin, same expiry as the mise/gomod go rule; matchDepNames golang scopes it to the toolchain image, not every dockerfile dep.

Majors across every manager in use need human review — gomod majors cross the /vN import-path boundary (import rewriting is a human job; +incompatible pre-SIV modules are the exception, gated uniformly anyway), and toolchain/image/npm majors otherwise arrive as ordinary auto-created PRs. Dashboard-gate rather than disable so security-relevant majors stay visible. Excludes go: the two rules above own the Go toolchain with their stricter allowedVersions pin. MUST stay before the automerge rules below.

Automerge: mise toolchain minor/patch/digest, excl. go. Kept as its own rule, not bolted onto the go-version gate rule, because automerge follows the same later-overwrites-earlier merge order as groupName — bolting it on would leak onto every matchPackageNames group above.

Automerge: gomod patch/digest, excl. go and the first-party group — matches only the go-patch group above (never go-minor, since that group never contains a patch/digest member). Must be the array's last rule in THIS preset — nothing after it can re-enable automerge for a group meant to stay manual. A downstream consumer that adds its own first-party matchers must exclude them here too, by appending a rule that sets automerge false for them (later rules overwrite earlier scalars).
